title: Ljus champinjonsås (Light Mushroom Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cream, mushrooms, and white pepper.
steps: Butter and flour are fried together, cream and mushroom broth are thinned in, and the sauce is allowed to simmer 10 minutes.
The mushrooms are cut in half and added, after which the sauce is seasoned with the spices.
Finally it is finished with the egg yolk, after which it must not boil further.

title: Lubsk medvurst (Lübeck Sausage)
description: Prepared with pork fat, beef, and pork.
steps: Cut the fat and meat the day before the sausage is to be made.
Cut the fat into 1 1/2 mm. cubes.
Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut into pieces, free from membranes and sinews, mix with 75 gr. of salt and let stand in a cold place until the following day.
Grind the meat 6 times through a meat grinder together with the meat juice, but after each time it passes through the grinder, spread out the forcemeat and let it cool.
Work the forcemeat vigorously together with spices and roe for about 45 minutes, then add the fat and work the forcemeat further for about 1/2 hour.
Stuff the forcemeat firmly into straight beef casings, and let the sausages hang in a cold place 4-6 days depending on the season.
Then hang in ordinary room temperature — in summer 5-6 hours, in winter 24-30 hours — to dry and become uniformly red.
Then cold-smoke for about 14 days.

title: Lungmos (Lung Puree)
description: Prepared with heart or pork, onion, and peppercorns.

ingredients.name: heart and lungs of calf, sheep or pork
ingredients.sourceText: heart and lungs of calf, sheep or pork

steps: The heart and lungs are cut up, rinsed and soaked in water for 12-15 hours, during which the water is changed 2 times.

They are placed in as much cold water as to just cover the meat, well skimmed and the seasonings are added; allowed to cook until tender, then the windpipe and air passages are cleaned away and the meat is chopped very finely.

Butter and flour are sautéed for 2 minutes, the well-skimmed broth is added, the meat is placed in it, the vinegar is added and the puree is allowed to cook while stirring for 10 minutes, after which it is carefully seasoned and served with boiled potatoes and vinegar.
If the puree is too thick, it is diluted with a little more broth; in the opposite case it is finished with a little potato flour, mixed in cold water, and then allowed to cook for 2 minutes.

title: Lungmos (Lung Purée)
description: Prepared with heart, onion, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: Heart offal of veal (lungs and heart)
ingredients.sourceText: Heart offal of veal (lungs and heart)

steps: Rinse the heart offal (lungs and heart) well and let it soak in cold water for about 12 hours so that the blood drains out.
Change the water at least three times.
Put the heart offal in cold water; when the stock comes to a boil, skim it carefully, then add the spices and the halved onion, and let the meat simmer slowly.
When it feels tender, remove it and strain the stock.
Cook the barley in the stock, and when it is almost done, add the finely chopped meat, and let everything cook until the barley is soft.
Season the purée to taste.

title: Lutfiskpudding (Lye Fish Pudding)
description: A pudding made with fish, rusks, and cream.

ingredients.name: finely chopped cooked lye fish (leftovers)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 liter finely chopped cooked lye fish (leftovers)

steps: Clarify the butter and mix with the crushed rusks
Add the lye fish along with the well-beaten eggs
Boil the milk and pour it hot over the mixture, then stir well
Season with salt, sugar and white pepper
Pour into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined pie form
Bake in oven until it has acquired a nice golden-brown color or approximately 40 minutes
Serve with clarified butter and small boiled potatoes

title: Lutning av fisk (Lye-Cured Fish)
description: A fish preparation using ling or saithe with lime, soda and water.
steps: Saw the fish into two or more pieces depending on size, and let it lie in cold water for a week, changing the water twice.
Brush it thoroughly clean with a scrub brush, especially on the skin side.

Spread a layer of lime in the bottom of a tub, then place the thickest fish pieces and sprinkle with lime, then fish again, and continue until all fish is laid down, but reserve about 4 dcl. of the lime to sprinkle over during the luring.
Pound the soda and dissolve it in 1 lit. lukewarm water.
Mix the soda solution with enough cold water that it stands over the fish.
Add it carefully around the edge of the tub so that the lime is not washed away from the fish.
As the fish swells, add more water and sprinkle a little more of the reserved lime.
The smallest pieces are usually ready after 2 days, the large ones after 4 days.
Remove them as they become ready and let them lie in fresh water for about 4 days, changing the water once a day.
This batch is sufficient for about 30 persons.

title: Lutning av fisk med soda (Luting of Fish with Soda)
description: Prepared with lime and water.
steps: The fish, which should be white in flesh, is cut into pieces and beaten well with a club.
Place the pieces in a tub with cold water (preferably seawater) and let them soak for a week, changing the water four times.
Dissolve the lime and soda in the cold water.
Place the fish in it with skin side up and place a weight on to keep the pieces down.
The fish should be turned often so that the pieces at the top come to the bottom.
After 3-4 days, take out the pieces as they become swollen.
Brush them with a root brush and place in cold water.
Change this water twice a day; during the first two days, brush the fish each time.
After about 8 days, the fish is ready to prepare.

title: Lökdolmar (Onion Dolmas)
description: Prepared with onions, veal, and white pepper.
steps: Peel the onion, place in boiling salted water and let cook slowly without a lid about 7 minutes.
Remove and carefully loosen the layers and place on linen to drain.
Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut into pieces and grind 3 times through a meat grinder.
Pound well in a mortar together with the butter and flour, then add the whipped egg and seasonings.
Work the forcemeat about 1/2 hour, adding the thin cream gradually, as the forcemeat easily breaks if done too quickly.
If it is too stiff, thin it with a little more cream.
Place a teaspoon of forcemeat on each onion layer, roll up and tie with cotton twine, first dipped in hot water.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the dolmas and brown nicely, then place the lid on and let braise slowly about 40 minutes.
Toward the end of cooking, add the broth.
Place on a warm platter, cut off the twine and pour the sauce over. Serve at the smörgåsbord.

title: Lökdolmar (Stuffed Onion Rolls, Serves 6)
description: A bread preparation made with onions, veal, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: For browning: 3 tablespoons butter (60 gr), 2 dcl broth
ingredients.sourceText: For browning: 3 tablespoons butter (60 gr), 2 dcl broth

steps: Peel the onion, place in boiling salted water and let simmer gently without a lid for about 7 minutes.
Remove the onion, carefully separate the leaves and place on linen to drain.
Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut into pieces and grind 3 times through a meat grinder.
Pound thoroughly in a mortar together with the butter and wheat flour, then add the beaten egg and seasonings.
Work the forcemeat for about 1/2 hour, adding the thin cream little by little, as the forcemeat can easily break otherwise.
If too stiff, dilute with a little more cream.
Place a teaspoon of forcemeat on each onion leaf, roll up and tie with cotton string previously dipped in hot water.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the dolmas and brown nicely, then put on the lid and let braise gently for about 40 minutes.
Toward the end of cooking add the broth.
Place on a warm platter, cut off the string and pour the sauce over them. Serve with the smörgåsbord.

title: Lübsk Medvurst (Lübeck Smoked Sausage)
description: Prepared with fat, beef, and pork.

ingredients.name: 32 gr. ground strong and white pepper
ingredients.sourceText: 32 gr. ground strong and white pepper

steps: Cut the fat and meat the day before the sausage is to be made.
Cut the fat into 1 1/2 mm. large dice.
Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut it into pieces, free it from membranes and sinews, mix with 75 gr. of the salt and let it stand in a cold place until the next day.
Grind the meat then 6 times through a meat grinder together with the meat juice, but after each time it is driven through the grinder, spread out the forcemeat and let it cool.
Work the forcemeat thereafter vigorously together with spices and roe for approximately 45 minutes, then add the fat and work the forcemeat further for approximately 1/2 hour.
Stuff the forcemeat tightly into straight beef casings, and let the sausages hang in a cold place for 4–6 days depending on the season.
Then let them hang in ordinary room temperature—in summer 5–6 hours, in winter 24–30 hours—to dry and become uniformly red.
Cold smoke thereafter for approximately 14 days.

title: Macaroni Croquettes (Makaronkroketter)
description: Prepared with macaroni, cream, and egg yolk.
steps: Break the macaroni into pieces, place in boiling salted water and cook until soft, about 20 minutes. Drain in a colander, rinse with cold water, drain on cloth and cut into 2 mm. thick rings.
Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream, and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes. Add the macaroni, stir in the egg yolk and season with the seasonings and cheese, if desired.

Spread the mixture on a flat dish buttered with butter, brush with a little butter so it does not dry, and let cool. Divide the mass into smaller portions—each portion should weigh about 35 gr.—which are rolled into elongated shapes on a floured board.
Dip the croquettes in the stiffly whipped eggs mixed with the table oil and seasoned with the seasonings, then roll in the crushed and sifted rusks and let sit for 1 hour to harden.
Fry golden-brown in hot lard and place on absorbent paper to drain. Serve with roasted meat.

title: Macaroni Gratin (for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with macaroni, béchamel, and onion.

ingredients.name: For the form: 1 tablespoon butter (20 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: For the form: 1 tablespoon butter (20 gr.)

steps: Break the macaroni into 4 cm. long pieces, place in boiling salted water and cook for about 20 minutes.
Strain in a colander, rinse with cold water and let drain.
For the sauce, fry the onion, meat, and flour (which should be dried in the oven) in the butter for about 10 minutes without browning.
Add the boiling milk, add the seasonings and let the sauce cook while stirring for 15 minutes, then strain through cloth and season.
Butter a fireproof form and sprinkle with ground breadcrumbs.
Layer the macaroni alternately with the sauce and grated cheese.
The top layer should be sauce, sprinkled with cheese and breadcrumbs.
Gratine the dish in a warm oven for about 15 minutes.
Serve as an intermediate course.

steps: Cook the macaroni as in the previous recipe but do not let it cool.

Fry the onion in half the butter, add the tomatoes and broth and cook until a purée forms, then strain.
Fry the remaining butter with the flour for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato purée, let the sauce cook for 5 minutes and season carefully with the seasonings.
Arrange the macaroni on a warm serving dish or in shells, sprinkle the cheese over and serve the sauce in a sauce bowl.

Garnish the dish with parsley and serve as an intermediate course.

title: Makaronikroketter (Macaroni Croquettes for 6 Servings)
description: Prepared with macaroni, cream, and egg yolk.
steps: Break the macaroni into pieces, place in boiling salted water and cook until soft, about 20 minutes.
Strain through a colander, rinse with cold water, drain on cloth and cut into 2 mm. thick rings.
Fry butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the macaroni, finish the stewing with the egg yolk and season with spices and cheese if desired.
Spread the stewing on a flat dish, grease with butter, brush with a little butter to prevent drying and let cool.
Divide the mass into smaller portions—each portion should weigh about 35 gr.—which are rolled into oblong shapes on a floured board.
Dip the croquettes in the stiffly beaten eggs mixed with cooking oil and seasoned with spices, then roll in the breadcrumbs and let rest for 1 hour to harden.
Fry golden-brown in hot lard and place on absorbent paper to drain.
Serve with roasted meat.

steps: Break the macaroni into pieces and rinse them.

title: Makaronipudding med Njurstuvning (Macaroni Pudding with Kidney Stew)
description: A pudding made with macaroni, breadcrumbs, and kidneys.
steps: Break the macaroni into 1 decimeter long pieces and parboil well in water.
Place them in a buttered and breadcrumb-covered ring mold.
Whisk the eggs together with the milk and seasonings, and pour this mixture over the macaroni.
Put the pudding in the oven to bake for 1 hour.
Blanch the kidneys and cut them into cubes, brown them in butter, add stock and let them cook until soft.
Melt butter and flour together, add meat gravy and stock, and let the sauce cook for 10 minutes.
Add the kidneys and season the stew with the spices and wine.
Turn the pudding out onto a plate, sprinkle the grated cheese over it, and place the stew in the middle.

title: Mandelberg (Almond Mound)
description: Prepared with almond, egg whites, and lemon juice.
steps: The almond is blanched, cut lengthwise into thin strips, which are lightly roasted in the oven and allowed to cool.
The egg whites are stirred together with the sugar and lemon juice for approximately 1 hour in the same direction, after which the almond is added.

Before the pastries are baked they can be sprinkled with 10 gr. blanched and finely pounded pistachios.
Instead of almond, 1 tablespoon cocoa can be added.

title: Mandelformar (Almond Forms)
description: Prepared with almond, egg yolks, and butter.
steps: Wash the butter and beat it with the sugar until it is white and fluffy, then add the blanched and ground almonds and the flour, and work the dough until it becomes even and smooth.
Let it thereafter stand in a cool place for approximately 2 hours.
Roll out the dough into a narrow rope, which is cut into pieces, with which small fluted pastry forms are lined internally.
Place the forms on a baking sheet, and bake the pastries in a not too hot oven until they are beautifully golden brown on both sides.
Take them out, turn them out immediately and let them cool on the turned-over forms.

title: Mandelspån (Almond Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with almond, powdered sugar, and egg whites.
steps: Each oblate sheet is divided into twelve equal, oblong rectangles.
Blanch the almonds, dry them in the oven, pass through an almond mill and pound together with the sugar and egg whites into a fine and smooth mass, to which more egg white is added if it is too hard.
Carefully spread the almond mass on the oblate and place the pastries on almond pastry forms and put in not too warm an oven to become light yellow and dry on the surface, but soft inside.

Remove them, let them cool, brush with the glaze (see no. 961) and immediately sprinkle with the blanched and finely chopped almonds and pistachios, as well as the orange peel and candied fruit cut into fine cubes, all well mixed together.
Let the pastries remain on the forms and put back in the oven so that the glaze dries and gets a beautiful light yellow color.

title: Mandelsås (Almond Sauce)
description: A sauce made with almonds, cream, and egg yolks.
steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them in the oven, grind them through an almond mill and pound them in a stone mortar with 2 teaspoons of cream to a fine paste.
Whisk the egg yolks and sugar for 20 minutes.
Heat the remaining cream with the almond paste and strain through muslin.
Heat the cream again and pour it over the egg mixture while whisking vigorously.
Let the sauce simmer with continued whisking until thick and foamy, then pour it out and whisk until cold.
Taste the sauce and, if desired, season with a little arrack, wine or liqueur, and it may also be colored green with spinach juice or red with carmine.

title: Mandeltårta (Almond Cake)
description: A cake made with almond, bitter almonds, and potato flour.
steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them and grind them. Dry the potato flour in a warm oven and let it cool.
Sift the sugar and stir with the egg yolks and water for about 1 hour, then add the almonds, the finely grated lemon zest and lemon juice, and the flour.

Last, carefully fold in the egg whites whipped to stiff peaks (see page 463), and fill the mixture into a buttered and breadcrumb-coated baking pan or cake form, and bake the tart in a not too hot oven for about 40 minutes.
Turn it up and let it cool, then split it into 2 bases, between which is placed vanilla or lemon cream or some fruit compote.
Glaze the tart (see recipe 961), prick with crystallized fruit and garnish with fruits and jelly.

title: Mannagrynskroketter (Semolina Croquettes for 6-8 Servings)
description: Prepared with semolina, egg yolk, and grated cheese.

ingredients.name: melted butter (20 gr.) for coating
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon melted butter (20 gr.) for coating

steps: Sift the semolina, rinse with cold water and drain.
Grease a pot with 1/2 tablespoon of butter, pour in the milk and bring to a boil.
Whisk in the semolina, then stir the porridge with a spoon until thickened, then move to a lower heat and let simmer slowly for about 20 minutes, stirring often.
Remove the porridge from heat, immediately blend with the remaining butter and let cool.
Add the beaten eggs, spices and grated cheese.
Grease a flat dish with butter, spread the mass on it about 2 cm. thick and let stand for 2-3 hours on ice to chill.

With a round mold, cut out small round cakes, place on a greased baking sheet, brush with butter, dust with a mixture of breadcrumbs and grated cheese and bake until nicely golden-brown in a warm oven.
Serve with roasted meat, for example venison.

title: Marinerad Grytstek (Marinated Pot Roast)
description: Prepared with chuck or steak, white pepper, and lard.

ingredients.name: inner loin or chuck steak
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 kg inner loin or chuck steak

steps: Lightly pound the meat with a damp mallet, dry it with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and rub it with the spices.
Peel and slice the onion and carrots, brown them in butter, and place half of them along with the parsley in a deep dish.
Place the meat on top and arrange the remaining vegetables, parsley, bay leaf, and pork broth on top of the meat.
Pour the wine over and let the roast marinate for about 6 hours, turning it 3-4 times.
Remove the meat, let it drain, dry it well with a cloth, cover it with lard slices and tie it so it has a nice shape.
Heat the lard in a cast iron pot, brown the roast on all sides until a nice brown crust forms, then remove it.
Pour out the lard and wipe the pot well with white paper.
Pour the marinade into the pot, place the meat on top, cover, and let the wine reduce rapidly until it has the consistency of syrup.

Add the boiling broth, which should reach the level of the meat (the pot should not be larger than necessary to fit the roast), cover and let the roast braise slowly for 2 1/2-3 hours, turning it several times but do not add liquid.
Place on a warm platter, garnish with parsley or kale, and slice at the table.
Serve with vegetables, browned potatoes, salads or potato pastries.
Strain the sauce, skim well, reduce if too thin or dilute if too thick, and add a little cream.

title: Marinerad grytstek (Marinated Pot Roast)
description: Prepared with white pepper, marinade, and carrots.
steps: The meat is lightly pounded with a damp mallet, dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and rubbed with the spices.

The onion and carrots are roasted, sliced, which are browned in butter, and half of them together with the parsley are laid in a deep dish, the meat is laid on top and the rest of the roots, the parsley, bay leaf and pork rinds are laid on top of the meat.
The wine is added and the roast is allowed to lie in this marinade for about 6 hours, during which time it is turned 3—4 times.
It is taken out, allowed to drip, dried well with a cloth, covered with fatback slices and tied so that it gets a beautiful shape.
The drippings are heated in an iron pot, the roast is browned in it on all sides until a beautiful brown crust is formed, then it is removed.

The drippings are discarded and the pot is cleaned well with white paper. The marinade is poured into the pot, the meat is laid on top, the lid is placed and the wine is allowed to boil rapidly until it gets the consistency of syrup.

Then the boiling broth is added, which should be level with the meat (the pot should not be larger than that the roast just fits neatly), the lid is placed on and the roast is allowed to roast slowly for 2 1/2—3 hours, during which time it is turned several times but is not moistened.
It is laid on a warm platter, garnished with parsley or kale and sliced at table. Served with vegetables, browned potatoes and salads or potato pastries.
The sauce is served as gravy or reduced (see no. 429).

title: Marinerad Grytstek (Marinated Pot Roast)
description: Prepared with beef or chuck or brisket, white pepper, and lard.
steps: Pound the meat lightly with a damp mallet, dry with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and rub with the spices.
Peel and chop the onions and carrots into slices, brown them in butter, and lay half of them along with the parsley in a deep pan.
Place the meat on top and lay the rest of the roots, parsley, bay leaf, and pork stock on top of the meat.
Add the wine and let the roast marinate for about 6 hours, turning it 3-4 times.
Remove the meat, let it drain, dry well with a cloth, lay the lard slices on top and tie it so it has a beautiful shape.
Heat the lard in an iron pot, brown the roast on all sides until a beautiful brown crust forms, then remove it.
Pour out the lard and scrub the pot well with white paper.
Pour the marinade into the pot, place the meat on top, cover, and let the wine reduce rapidly until it has the consistency of syrup.

Then add the boiling broth, which should be level with the meat (the pot should be only just large enough for the roast), cover and let the meat braise slowly for 2.5-3 hours, turning it a few times but do not add liquid.
Place the roast on a warm platter, garnish with parsley or kale and carve at the table.
Serve with vegetables, browned potatoes and salads or potato pastries.
Serve the sauce as gravy or reduced (see no. 429).

title: Marinerad Oxhare (Marinated Beef Hare)
description: Prepared with beef, fat, and marinade or red wine.

ingredients.name: For the marinade: 2 dcl white or red wine
ingredients.sourceText: For the marinade: 2 dcl white or red wine

steps: The beef hare, which should have hung 4–8 days depending on the season, is prepared and larded (see page 232), and placed in a crock.
For the marinade all ingredients are mixed well, then poured over the meat, which is left to marinate 2–3 days and should be turned often during this time.
The meat is taken out, dried well, tied so it takes on a beautiful shape, and braised as in recipe 474.
It is moistened first with 2 dcl of the strained marinade, sprinkled with sugar, covered with the anchovy and thereafter the cream is added gradually.
Served with browned potatoes and reduced sauce (see recipe 429), mixed with 1 tbsp chopped capers or 2 tbsp currant jelly.

title: Marinerad Svinkarré (Marinated Pork Loin)
description: Prepared with white pepper, red wine, and salt.
steps: Free the loin from most of the fat, rub it with a mixture of salt and pepper and place it in a deep dish.
Add the red wine and let the loin soak in it about 12 hours, turning it several times.
Brown the butter in a long pan, place the loin in it with the meat side up and brown it in a hot oven, basting it frequently.
Add the marinade and let it roast until tender, or about 1 1/2 hours.
Cut as in recipe no. 561, serve with a roux-based sauce (see no. 429) mixed with cream and with browned potatoes and lingonberry jelly or preserved rowan berries.

title: Marinerade lammkotletter (Marinated Lamb Chops)
description: Prepared with lamb chops, lard, and beef tongue.

ingredients.name: applesauce with 30 gr. grated finely chopped horseradish, or mushrooms sliced and sautéed in butter
ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups applesauce with 30 gr. grated finely chopped horseradish, or mushrooms sliced and sautéed in butter

steps: Prepare the chops as in the previous recipe, lard with lard and tongue cut into fine strips, rub with the seasonings and place on a dish.
Sprinkle with onion, finely cut parsley stems and bay leaves, and pour over lemon juice and cooking oil.
Marinate for 1/2 hour, turning 4 times.
Remove (shake off the seasonings), wrap in cloth, dip in melted butter and turn in crushed breadcrumbs.
Fry the chops as in the previous recipe, arrange in a circle on a hot serving dish.
Whisk the pan with boiling bouillon and pour the sauce over the chops.
Garnish the center of the dish with applesauce mixed with grated finely chopped horseradish, or with mushrooms sliced and sautéed in butter.
Garnish around with parsley or salad.
Serve with French potatoes or potato mousse flowers.

title: Marinerade Oxrulader (Marinated Beef Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with beef, lard, and onion.
steps: Prepare the meat as in the previous recipe, cut into 12 slices, beat them well, place on a platter, pour the marinade over them and let them rest 1 hour, turning them once.
Mix all ingredients for the marinade and add, if desired, 1/2 tbsp finely chopped onion.
Cut the lard into 12 strips, which are rolled in a mixture of the onion, parsley and anchovy sauce.
Wrap the meat slices in cloth, and on each one place a strip of lard, then roll the meat slices up tightly and bind with fine sailcloth yarn or fasten together with toothpicks.
Heat a frying pan, brown the butter in it, add the rolls and brown them nicely all around, then place them in a warm iron pot.
Fry the flour with the butter in the frying pan, add the boiling stock or water together with the wine, and let the sauce come to a good boil and pour it over the rolls.
Let them thereafter slowly cook with a tightly closed lid until tender, or about 2-2 1/2 hours.
Place them on warm carrots, taste the sauce and pour it over.
Serve with pressed potatoes or potato puree.

title: Marinerade Oxrulader (Marinated Swedish Beef Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with lard, onion, and anchovy.
steps: The meat is treated as in the previous recipe, cut into 12 slices, which are well beaten, placed on a platter, covered with the marinade and allowed to lie 1 hour, during which they are turned once.
All the marinade ingredients are well mixed together and combined, if desired, with 1/2 tablespoon finely chopped onion.
The lard is cut into 12 strips, which are rolled in a mixture of the onion and parsley and the anchovy sauce.
The meat slices are removed from the marinade, the lard strips are placed on each slice, and the rolls are tightly rolled up and bound or fastened as in recipe 480.
The rolls are well browned in butter and sprinkled with flour; the broth or water mixed with wine is poured on, and they are allowed to simmer slowly with a tight lid, 2 1/2–3 hours.
They are placed on a warm platter, the strings are cut away, the sauce is whisked well, thinned if necessary, tasted and poured over the rolls.
Served with boiled potatoes.

title: Marinerat fårkott (Marinated Mutton Roast)
description: Prepared with mutton, lard, and white pepper.
steps: The roast should have hung so that it is tender. The knuckle and the thin part are trimmed away and the roast is larded (see page 232) with strips of lard, dipped in a mixture of the salt, pepper and ginger, and placed in a deep dish.

It is removed and allowed to cool, cut into thin slices and garnished with stuffed eggs (see no. 8) as well as green salad or parsley and served with mayonnaise.

title: Marinerat Rådjur (Marinated Roebuck)

title: Marmeladpudding (Marmalade Pudding)
description: A pudding made with marmalade, melted butter, and cream.

ingredients.name: hot water for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp. hot water for the pan

steps: Melt the sugar in a pan, add the water, and line a heatproof pan with this mixture.
Mix the marmalade well with the butter.
Whip the egg yolks with the cream and mix with the crushed rusks and biscuits.
Add the egg mixture to the marmalade, a little at a time, and stir the mixture well.
Finally, carefully fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Fill the mixture into the lined pan and bake the pudding in a water bath in the oven approximately 1 hour.
Serve warm or cold with vanilla sauce.

title: Maränger (Meringues)
description: Prepared with egg whites, almond, and powdered sugar.
steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them well and chop them very finely.
Sift the sugar through a fine sieve.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and carefully blend the sugar with a fork into the egg white foam.
Pipe with a smooth piping tube or with two teaspoons onto a well buttered baking sheet in wreaths or round balls, which are sprinkled with the almonds and sugar.
Bake the meringues in gentle oven heat until they are yellow and hard on the surface but not completely dry.
Loosen them with a knife from the sheet while they are warm.

title: Marängpyramid med Frusen Grädde (Meringue Pyramid with Frozen Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, egg whites, and pears.
steps: Cut 6 strips from stiff paper and form them into rings of different sizes, the first being 12 cm in diameter, each of the others 1 cm smaller than the preceding one
Butter the paper rings with washed butter or with salad oil, and on the outer side press the meringue batter through a piping bag in the form of meringues side by side
The size of the meringues decreases according to the size of the papers
The last paper should be a round disk on which some leaves are formed with the piping bag
Sprinkle the meringues with sugar and bake in a mild oven heat, remove and let cool
Carefully remove the paper so that the meringues do not break
Then arrange wreath upon wreath until they form a pyramid
Cut the canned pears into pieces
Whip the cream together with sugar until stiff peaks form, mix in the pears with their syrup, and freeze the cream
Fill the pyramid with this and garnish with whipped cream beaten to stiff peaks and colored with a little carmine

title: Marängsuisse (Meringue Cake)
description: A cake made with icing sugar, egg whites, and cream.
steps: Sift the sugar through a fine sieve.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and carefully fold in the sugar with a fork into the egg white foam.

Spread the mixture on a well-cleaned and buttered sheet in the form of round bases, which should be uniform if the meringue cake is to be made cylindrical, but larger and smaller if a pyramidal shape is desired.
Pipe a ring of small meringues close together around the edge of each base.
Dust the meringues lightly with sugar and bake in gentle oven heat until they are almost dry and release from the sheet, or about 1 hour.
Whip the cream with the sugar to stiff peaks, then add the vanilla sugar.
When the meringue cakes are cold, layer them together with cream between each.
Cover the outside of the cake with whipped cream, smoothed flat with a spoon.
Divide the remaining cream into two parts; color one part pink with a little dissolved carmine.
Pipe the white and pink cream through a fluted piping bag in beautiful garlands over the cake.
Carefully transfer to a flat glass dish with parchment paper.
The meringue cake should not be decorated until 1/2 hour before it is to be served.
The meringue cake can be decorated with only white cream and preserved fruits if desired.

title: Marängsuisse (Meringue Suisse)
description: Prepared with egg whites, powdered sugar, and cream.
steps: Beat the egg whites until stiff and continue beating for about 15 minutes.
Then carefully fold in the sifted powdered sugar.
Pour the mixture into piping bags with closed tips and pipe onto well-cleaned and buttered baking sheets, ring by ring, so that these together form wreaths.
Make the wreaths larger and smaller so that they, laid one upon the other, form a pyramid.
Place them in gentle oven heat and bake very slowly until they release from the sheet.
When they are cold, arrange them on a glass bowl, wreath upon wreath, into a pyramid.
Whip the cream with vanilla sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fill and coat the pyramid with whipped cream.
Divide the remaining cream in two; color one part with carmine to a beautiful pink color, and with this and the white cream garnish the pyramid through piping bags.

If the rings are made the same size, one can make a muff from them, fill it inside with pink cream and coat it with white cream. A little chocolate is dissolved in cream, and with this the muff is garnished, so that it resembles an ermine muff.

Gently fold in the previously sifted granulated sugar
Place the batter in piping bags and pipe onto well-cleaned and buttered baking sheets in rings, so that these together form wreaths
Make the wreaths in different sizes so that when laid on top of each other they form a pyramid
Place them in a mild oven heat and bake very slowly until they release from the sheet
When cool, arrange them on a glass dish, wreath upon wreath, into a pyramid
Whip the cream with vanilla sugar until stiff peaks form
Fill and coat the pyramid with whipped cream
Divide the remaining cream in two parts; color one part with carmine to a beautiful pink color, and with this and the white cream garnish the pyramid using piping bags

title: Marängsuisse (Meringue Tower)
description: Prepared with icing sugar, egg whites, and cream.
steps: Sift the sugar through a fine sieve.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and carefully fold in the sugar with a fork into the egg white foam.

Spread the mixture onto a well-cleaned and buttered sheet in the form of round bases, which should be uniform if the meringue tower is to be made cylindrical, but larger and smaller if the tower is desired to be pyramid-shaped.
On the edge of each base, pipe a ring of small meringues, close together.
Dust the meringues with a little sugar and bake in gentle oven heat until they are almost dry and release from the sheet, approximately 1 hour.
Whip the cream with the sugar to stiff peaks, then add the vanilla sugar.
When the meringue cakes are cold, layer them together with cream between each.
Cover the tower externally with whipped cream, smoothing it even with a spoon.
Divide the remaining cream in two parts; color one part pink with a little dissolved carmine.
Pipe the white and pink cream through a fluted piping tube in beautiful garlands over the tower, then carefully transfer it to a flat glass dish with parchment paper.
Do not decorate the meringue tower until 1/2 hour before it is to be served.
It may be decorated with only white cream and preserved fruits if desired.

title: Marängsuisse med choklad (Meringue Cake with Chocolate)
description: A cake made with chocolate, icing sugar, and egg whites.
steps: Prepare the meringue mixture as in the previous recipe and shape into small rings or regular meringues on a well-cleaned and buttered sheet.
Dust lightly with sugar and bake in gentle oven heat until they are almost completely dry and release from the sheet.
Dissolve the chocolate in a water bath without adding water.
Blanch the almonds, cut them into thin slices, and lightly roast them with 2 tsp. sugar in the oven.
When the meringues are cold, layer them on a flat glass dish with parchment paper, alternating with the melted chocolate so that they form a pyramid.
Pour chocolate over the pyramid and sprinkle with the roasted almonds.
Whip the cream with the sugar to stiff peaks.
Flavor half of it with vanilla sugar; color the other half pink with carmine.
Pipe the white and pink cream separately through a fluted piping bag in beautiful garlands over the pyramid.
The cake should not be decorated until 1/2 hour before it is to be served.

title: Mazariner (Mazarines)
description: Prepared with icing sugar, egg yolk, and wheat flour.
steps: Wash the butter and beat it with the sugar until white and fluffy, then beat in the egg yolk; lastly add the flour sifted with the baking powder, then let the dough rest for about 2 hours.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut out into rounds with a mold to line buttered pastry molds.
For the filling, blanch the almond and grind through an almond mill.
Beat the eggs and sugar for 15 minutes, then add the almond.
If desired, place a little strawberry jam in the bottom of the molds.
Fill the molds almost to the brim with almond paste and bake in a not-too-hot oven until the almond paste, when tested with a whisk, feels dry.
If desired, the pastries may be glazed with water glaze (recipe no. 961).

title: Medvurst (Smoked Sausage)
description: Prepared with beef, pork, and lard.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in cold water and cut into pieces.
Remove sinews and membranes and pass the meat 5 times through the meat grinder.
Cut the lard into fine, even cubes.
Work the ground meat alone for ½ hour.
Then mix in the finely ground spices, sugar, potassium nitrate (likewise finely ground), cognac, and pork cubes.
Work the mixture for another ½ hour.
Stuff the forcemeat as tightly as possible into straight ox casings with the tallow side turned out.
Tie the finished sausages, rub them with salt, sugar, and potassium nitrate and let them lie for 3 days.
Turn them morning and evening and rub in with salt, sugar, and potassium nitrate each time.
Smoke the sausages for 3 days.
Store them hanging in a cool place or packed in juniper branches.

title: Mellanrätt av Nudel (Creamed Noodles for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with noodles, cream, and white pepper.
steps: Bring the water to a boil with salt in a large pot and add the noodles, letting them cook about 15 minutes.
Pour into a colander and let the water drain well.
Melt the butter in the pot, add the noodles and add the cream gradually while the stew cooks for about 1 hour.
Season with the spices, arrange on plates, sprinkle with cheese and serve very hot.

Mushroom stew can also be mixed in. The mixture can also be placed in a buttered and breadcrumb-lined mold, gratinéed in a water bath in the oven and turned out onto a platter, though the stew should then be slightly firmer.

title: Melonkompott (Melon Compote)
description: Prepared with melon, rum, and citron.
steps: The melon, which should be ripe, is cut into 1 cm thick slices and these are cut into 5 cm long pieces.
Place the cut melon in 1 liter of boiling water and cook for 2-3 minutes, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on cloth.
Make a clear, syrupy syrup from the sugar, water, rum and lemon juice.
Add the melon and cook until it is soft and clear.
Place it in a compote bowl; if desired, cook down the syrup and pour it over.
Serve cold with biscuits.

title: Moir's vingelé (Moir's Wine Jelly)
description: Prepared with jelly, juice, and wine or sherry.
steps: Stir the jelly powder, sugar, lemon juice and water in a bowl until the powder and sugar are dissolved, then add the wine and pour the mixture into a large or several small molds rinsed with water and sprinkled with sugar and let it set on ice for 4-5 hours.

This jelly can advantageously be colored red and used as garnish for cold rice pudding. A light, fine sponge cake can be soaked through with this jelly, which should then be heated to approximately 60 degrees. The jelly then sets. The cake is served whole, or cut into slices, with whipped cream.

description: Prepared with lemon or vanilla or sugar, egg yolks, and milk.

ingredients.name: zest of 1/2 lemon or 1 tbsp. vanilla sugar

title: Mondaminpudding med vin (Mondamin Pudding with Wine)
description: A pudding made with wine, citron, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: skal och saft av 1/2 citron (zest and juice of 1/2 lemon)
ingredients.sourceText: skal och saft av 1/2 citron (zest and juice of 1/2 lemon)

steps: Mix the mondamin flour with 1 dcl. of the water.
Boil the remaining water with the sugar and the lemon zest and juice.
Add the wine and the mondamin mixture and let the cream boil for 5 minutes.
Remove the pan from heat and whisk in the egg yolks one at a time.
Let the cream simmer under vigorous whisking until thick, then remove from heat and continue whisking until the cream is cold.
Rinse a nice metal mold with cold water and sprinkle with granulated sugar.
Pour the cream into the mold and let it sit on ice for 2-3 hours.
Unmold the pudding onto a flat glass dish and garnish with ladyfingers or macaroons.

title: Mormors fina tårta (Grandmother's Fine Cake)
description: A cake made with clarified butter, wheat flour, and rusks.

ingredients.name: washed butter for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons crushed rusks for the pan

steps: Beat the egg yolks together with the sugar for half an hour.
Clarify the butter and set it out to cool.
Stir it until it becomes white and fluffy, then blend it into the egg mixture.
Add the sifted wheat flour and then the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the batter into a buttered and rusk-sprinkled pan or mold and bake in fairly good oven heat.
When the cake has cooled, cut it into two layers and fill with cream or applesauce.
Glaze and garnish with fruit and crystallized sugar.

title: Morotpuré (Carrot Purée)
description: Prepared with carrots, broth, and egg yolks.
steps: Brush the carrots, rinse, scrape, rinse again, dry and cut into cubes, which are browned in half of the butter.
Add 1 liter of the boiling broth and let the carrots cook until they are quite soft, then strain.
Fry the rest of the butter with the flour 2 minutes.
Add the purée and the remaining broth and let the soup cook 5 minutes.
Season with the spices.
Whisk the egg yolks and cream in a soup bowl, pour in the purée while whisking and serve with toasted bread or cheese croutons.

title: Mosspudding (Moss Pudding)
description: A pudding made with egg yolks, sherry, and juice.
steps: Mix the egg yolks, wine, sugar, finely grated lemon zest and lemon juice in a saucepan and whip until the sugar melts.
Let the cream then simmer over the fire with vigorous whisking until it is thick and foamy, then remove from heat and continue whisking until the cream is cold.
Rinse the gelatin in cold water and dissolve it in the hot water.
Whip the cream until stiff peaks form.
First add the gelatin to the cream, then fold in the cream very carefully.
Fill the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-dusted mold and let it sit on ice for 3-4 hours.
When the pudding is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife, turn it out onto a flat glass plate lined with parchment paper and garnish with cookies.

title: Mosspudding med Mandel (Almond Moss Pudding)
description: A pudding made with sweet almonds, bitter almonds, and gelatin.
steps: The almonds are blanched, grated and pounded together with the sugar into a fine paste.
The almond paste, milk and eggs are whipped together in a pot and the mixture is simmered over heat while whipping until the cream thickens.
The gelatin dissolved in a little lukewarm water is added, and when the mixture is cold, the cream whipped to stiff peaks is stirred in.
The cream is poured into a rinsed and sugared mold and set out to stiffen.
When it is to be served, the mold is held for a moment in lukewarm water, the pudding is turned out and garnished with jam and biscuits.

title: Muslinsförs av vilt (Mousseline Forcemeat of Game)
description: Prepared with hare, white pepper, and egg yolk.

ingredients.name: 1 large hare, approximately 450 gr. scraped meat
ingredients.sourceText: 1 large hare, approximately 450 gr. scraped meat

steps: Skin and clean the hare. Cut off head, paws and slaughter sides, then rinse the hare very well, dry it and remove all membranes.
Cut all meat loose from the bones, scrape it free from sinews and membranes, mix with the seasonings and pass 6 times through a meat grinder.
Pound the forcemeat thereafter in a stone mortar with a wooden pestle until it becomes even and smooth, then add the whipped egg and egg yolk with vigorous stirring.
Pass the forcemeat through a hair sieve, place in a mold or smaller saucepan, which is set in a bowl with ice and let it stand 1 hour, or until it is completely cooled.
Stir it then, let it remain on the ice and add the cream a little at a time with even and vigorous stirring.
Test the forcemeat as in the previous recipe.
Forcemeat prepared in this way is especially fine and delicate and is well suited for finer side dishes, garnishes, etc.
Meat of veal, fowl, game birds, fish and shellfish can be used for this.

title: Märgpudding (Beef Marrow Pudding)
description: A pudding made with beef marrow, kidney, and bread crumbs.

ingredients.name: 1 hg. preserved fruit, in fine cubes
ingredients.sourceText: 1 hg. preserved fruit, in fine cubes

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 gr.) for the mold

ingredients.name: wheat flour (20 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp. wheat flour (20 gr.) for the mold

steps: The marrow and fat are cleaned well, rinsed, wrapped in a cloth, placed in a colander, melted in a water bath, and the fat is allowed to cool.
Bread crumbs are weighed, soaked in the milk and wrung out.

The fat is worked well with the sugar, the wrung-out bread, the whipped eggs, the egg yolks, the fruit cubes, the cleaned and rinsed sultana raisins and the cleaned, rinsed, split and pitted Malaga raisins.
The mixture is poured into a buttered and floured smooth ring mold and baked in a water bath in the oven for about 1 hour.
Serve warm, covered with hot wine sauce (see no. 457), mixed with rum or with flaming sauce (see no. 465), which is ignited when the pudding is brought to the table.

title: Mörk Buljong (Dark Broth)
description: A soup made with beef or marrow, veal, and carrot.

ingredients.name: beef rib or marrow pipe
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 kg. beef rib or marrow pipe

ingredients.name: 3 hectograms lean, boneless beef for clarification
ingredients.sourceText: 3 hectograms lean, boneless beef for clarification

ingredients.name: 1 egg white and the rinsed eggshells for clarification
ingredients.sourceText: 1 egg white and the rinsed eggshells for clarification

steps: Prepare the meat as in recipe no. 222 and cut it from the bones into small pieces.
Crush the bones as finely as possible and brown them well in half of the butter in a frying pan together with the prepared and chopped vegetables and the onion.
Place the browned bones in the broth pot and deglaze the frying pan with a little boiling water, which is then poured into the pot.
Add the cold water and parsley, and set the broth over fresh fire to boil rapidly.
When the boiling point is reached, skim it well, wipe the edge, place the lid on and let the broth cook slowly for 4 hours.
During this time, brown the meat in the remaining butter; when the bones have cooked 4 hours, add the meat and let everything cook for an additional 3 hours.
Treat the broth as in the previous recipe and serve with the same kinds of garnish.
The dark broth is used advantageously for à-la-daube of game, poultry in aspic, chaud-froid, etc., but not for prepared soups and purées.

title: Njursauté (Kidney Sauté)
description: Prepared with kidneys, white pepper, and mushrooms.
steps: Blanch the kidneys, that is, place them in cold salted water, let them come to a boil and boil uncovered for 3-4 minutes, after which they are placed on a sieve and allowed to cool.
Slice them thinly, sprinkle with the spices and turn in the flour.
Slice the mushrooms.
Heat the butter in a pan: when it is light brown, add the kidney and mushroom slices and brown them evenly while shaking.
Dilute with the broth and let the stew boil for 5 minutes, after which the wine is added and the sauté is allowed to cook an additional 8-10 minutes.
Serve as a breakfast dish with fried potatoes.

title: Njursoppa (Kidney Soup)
description: A soup made with beef kidneys, meat, and white pepper.
steps: Cut the kidneys and meat into small cubes and season with pepper and salt. Peel the onion, chop it finely and fry it together with the meat in butter for about 10 minutes.
Add the flour together with the rice grains, parsley bunch and broth. When the meat is completely tender, strain the soup and skim off the fat carefully.
Press the meat and kidneys through a fine sieve. Mix the pressed mixture into the soup, which is then brought to a boil.
If desired, add a little wine or curry powder to the soup. Serve with toasted bread.

title: Nougatkräm (Nougat Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, sweet almonds, and egg yolks.
steps: Blanch and finely chop the almonds. Place the granulated sugar in a slightly warm frying pan, greased with {{source-2}}, and stir with a wooden spoon over heat until melted. Add the almonds immediately, and let the mixture come to a boil and pour onto a well-cleaned and buttered baking sheet. As soon as the nougat has cooled slightly, cut it into even squares with a greased knife and loosen from the sheet. Crush half of the nougat finely in a mortar; save the other half for garnish.

For the cream, beat the egg yolks and sugar for 15 minutes. Heat the thin cream with the vanilla and pour it in with vigorous whisking onto the beaten egg yolks, then let the cream simmer over heat with continued whisking. Remove the pan and whisk the cream until it is cold, then add the rinsed gelatin dissolved in the hot water and the crushed nougat. Last, carefully fold in the cream beaten to stiff peaks. Pour the cream into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled mold and let it set on ice for approximately 3 hours. When the cream is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a flat glass plate with parchment paper. Garnish with the remaining nougat and grapes, and macaroons if desired.

Place the sugar in a slightly warm pan, greased with {{source-2}}, and stir with a wooden spoon over heat until melted.
Add the almonds at once and bring to a boil, then pour onto a well-cleaned and greased baking sheet.
When the nougat has cooled somewhat, cut it into even squares with a hack knife, grease with butter, and loosen from the sheet.
Finely crush half of the nougat in a stone mortar; reserve the other half for garnish.
For the cream, beat the egg yolks and sugar for 15 minutes.
Heat the thin cream with the vanilla bean and whip it vigorously into the beaten egg yolks.
Allow the cream to simmer over heat with continued whisking.
Remove the pan from heat and whisk the cream until cold.
Add the rinsed gelatin that has been dissolved in the hot water and the crushed nougat.
Last, gently fold in the cream that has been whipped to stiff peaks.
Pour the cream into a rinsed and sugar-sprinkled mold and let it stand on ice for about 3 hours.
When the cream is to be served, loosen it from the edges with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a flat glass dish with parchment paper.
Garnish with the remaining nougat and grapes, and macaroons if desired.

title: Nougatpudding (Nougat Pudding)
description: A pudding made with sweet almonds, hazelnut, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: 2 hg. spanska ell. hasselnötter (Spanish or hazelnut)
ingredients.sourceText: 2 hg. spanska ell. hasselnötter (Spanish or hazelnut)

ingredients.name: 3 msk. varmt vatten, till gelatinet (warm water for the gelatin)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 msk. varmt vatten, till gelatinet (warm water for the gelatin)

steps: Blanch the almonds and dry them in the oven.
Peel the nuts and chop them finely together with the almonds.
Whisk the whole egg and egg yolks well in a bowl.
Place the sugar in a buttered and slightly warm pan and stir with a wooden spoon over heat until melted.
Immediately add the almonds and nuts to the melted sugar, let it come to a boil, and pour under stirring onto the whisked eggs.
Rinse the gelatin in cold water, cut it into pieces, dissolve it in the warm water and add it.
Stir the mixture until it is cold, then fold in the cream beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled mold and let it set on ice for 2-3 hours.
When the pudding is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife and unmold onto a flat glass dish with parchment paper.
Garnish with candied nuts and ladyfingers.

title: Nudel (Egg Noodle Dough)
description: Prepared with cream, clarified butter, and eggs.

ingredients.name: flour, as much as needed for a firm dough
ingredients.sourceText: flour, as much as needed for a firm dough

steps: Whisk the eggs with the cream for 10 minutes.
Add the butter and stir in as much flour as needed to make a properly firm dough.
Roll out the dough to the thickness of a coin and let it rest in a cold room to stiffen overnight.
Spread it out into strips 1 1/2 cm. wide, which are cut across into fine ribbons.
Let these dry well and they can be stored for several weeks in a tin box with a tightly closed lid.

title: Nyponkräm (Rose Hip Cream)
description: Prepared with rose hips, potato flour, and water.
steps: Rinse the rose hips, place them in cold water and let them cook slowly for about 2 hours.
During cooking, stir them vigorously a few times to extract the flavor.
Pass the rose hips, return the juice to the heat with sugar and cinnamon.
When it boils, skim carefully and thicken the cream with potato flour mixed in a little cold water, then give it a short boil.
Pour into a jelly mold to cool and serve with whipped cream.

title: Nyponsoppa (Rose Hip Soup)
description: A soup made with rose hips, potato flour, and raisins or prunes.
steps: Rinse the rose hips well in lukewarm water and let them drain.
Set them on to boil in the cold water and let them cook soft for about 1 1/2 hours; during this time whisk the soup often so that the rose hips fall apart.
Strain them, add the sugar, bring the soup to boil, skim it, and thicken it with the potato flour, stirred in 1/2 kkp cold water.
Let the soup cook 2 minutes, season it, and serve with the rinsed and cooked raisins or plums, the blanched and thinly sliced almond, and whipped cream.

title: Nässelkål (Nettle Soup)
description: A soup made with chives, chervil or fennel, and meat.

ingredients.name: 1 handful chervil or 1/2 teaspoon ground fennel
ingredients.sourceText: 1 handful chervil or 1/2 teaspoon ground fennel

steps: The nettles are cleaned and rinsed very thoroughly
They are pre-boiled for 15 minutes as in recipe no. 257, placed on a sieve, rinsed with cold water and left to drain well
The chervil and chives are cleaned, rinsed, wrung in a cloth and chopped finely together with the nettles, after which they are passed through a sieve
Butter, nettles and flour are fried for 5 minutes, the boiling broth is thinned, little by little, and the soup is allowed to cook with the lid slightly ajar for about 1/2 hour
It is carefully seasoned with spices (with fennel, if chervil is lacking) and served with fish forcemeat quenelles, poached eggs or egg dumplings
Preserved nettles can be used advantageously
The soup can be prepared in the same way from chopped, preserved spinach

title: Nässelkål med förlorade ägg (Nettle Cabbage with Poached Eggs)
description: Prepared with chives, broth, and white pepper.
steps: Clean the nettles well, rinse them and blanch them in salted boiling water for approximately 15 minutes.
Drain the water, rinse the nettles with fresh water, and lay them on a sieve to drain.
Chop the nettles finely together with the cleaned and rinsed chives and sprinkle with flour.
Fry them in the butter, and add the hot broth.
Let the cabbage now cook very slowly with a tightly closed lid for approximately 3/4 hour.
Skim well, season with the spices and serve with poached eggs.

title: Olivsås (Olive Sauce)

title: Omelett i form (Baked Omelette Mould)
description: Prepared with stock, cream, and butter.

ingredients.name: butter (10 grams) for the mould

steps: Pat the chanterelles in a cloth, cut them into slices, and sauté in butter until clear.
Squeeze the mushroom out of the butter with a spoon.
Sauté the flour with butter for 2 minutes, then add the chanterelle stock and cream. Let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushroom back, season the ragout with the spices, place it in a buttered omelette mould.
Whisk the egg mixture well and pour it over the ragout.
Bake the omelette in the oven and serve at the smorgasbord. Instead of the ragout, smoked ham cut into cubes and sautéed in butter, or grated cheese can be used.

title: Omelett med hummerstuvning (Omelet with Lobster Stew)
description: Prepared with lobster, cream, and white pepper.
steps: Separate the egg yolks and whites.
Whisk the yolks together with the cream, salt and sugar (if using), and fold in the egg whites beaten until stiff.
Pour the batter into a well-buttered omelet pan and bake light yellow in ordinary oven heat.
Tip the omelet out immediately, place the stew on half of the omelet, and fold the other half over.
For the stew, fry the butter and flour together, and add the cream with constant stirring.
Let the sauce boil for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped lobster and season the stew.
Finally stir in the whisked egg yolk.

title: Omelett med Potatis och Skinka (Omelet with Potato and Ham)

Cut the potato into slices and the ham into oblong rectangular pieces.
Peel, chop, and fry the onion in butter.
Butter an omelet pan, layer the potato, ham, and onion in it, and pour the egg mixture over.
Shake the pan over the heat until the omelet has set, then turn it out first onto a lid and then onto the serving plate so the unbaked side comes up.
Sprinkle the omelet with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

title: Omelett med Stuvade Murklor och Champinjoner (Omelet with Stewed Mushrooms and Button Mushrooms)

title: Orange Marmalade II (Apelsinmarmelad II)
description: Prepared with oranges, orange, and sugar.

ingredients.name: sugar equal in weight to the mass
ingredients.sourceText: sugar equal in weight to the mass

steps: Wash the oranges well, dry them, place them whole in plenty of cold water and let them cook until they are so soft that they can be pierced with a fine whisk.
When they have cooled, press out the fruit flesh from the peel with a silver spoon.
Remove the pips carefully, and cut the peels into very fine strips.
Scrape the fruit flesh somewhat, removing the coarsest membranes.
Mix together the peel, fruit flesh and 1 litre of the liquid in which the oranges were cooked, weigh it, and take an equal weight of fine sugar.
Let the mass cook for 1 hour before adding the sugar, and let the marmalade cook thereafter about 45 minutes, or until it is clear and of proper consistency.
Pour it into small warm glass jars, previously rinsed with brandy.
Bind the jars when the marmalade is cold.
If a less bitter marmalade is desired, remove the peels from 3 oranges.
